small_guidance:
- The kernel currently puts each (kh,kw) outside the C_in reduction loop, forcing 9 separate K loops with redundant load/dot setup. Restructure so BLOCK_K spans C_in*KH*KW (or at least merges the kw axis), giving longer accumulator chains and better dot utilization.
- Drop the over-large autotune configs (e.g. 256×64 BLOCK_K=32, 128×128 BLOCK_K=64) which exceed the 132KB SMEM budget on Ampere fp32 and never get selected; add a 128×64 BLOCK_K=32 num_warps=4 stages=3 config which tends to win for OC=128, HW=15876.
- Cache the NHWC permuted input across calls if the agent harness reuses x, or fuse the input permute into the kernel by indexing NCHW directly with strided loads along C (still coalesced when BLOCK_K covers C_in=64 in one shot).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a true implicit-GEMM where the K-dimension is C_in*KH*KW unrolled (size 576 here) with a single inner loop, one program per (N, OC tile, HW_out tile). This removes the 9× loop overhead and lets BLOCK_K=32 or 64 deliver full tensor-core-style mma throughput.
- Stay in NCHW input layout but produce NHWC accumulation: load weights as [C_out, C_in*KH*KW] (precomputed once), and gather x via (n, ic, oh+kh, ow+kw) offsets computed from the flattened K index — avoids the up-front NHWC permute of the activation (a heavy memcpy each forward).
- Write the output directly in NCHW by swapping the store offset math (store per-OC stripe as contiguous HW), eliminating the trailing `.permute(0,3,1,2).contiguous()` which is currently a large extra pass over the 64×128×126×126 tensor.
